title: Debt and Deadline
premise: Jonah Blackwood, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map — is pulled back into service when a burner phone rings with the voice of his dead mentor, Elias Voss, who faked his death two years ago. Voss offers Jonah the one secret worth killing for: proof of who inside Meridian ordered a massacre in Lagos that Jonah helped cover up. As rival fixers, a vengeful widow, and Meridian's own cleaners close in, Jonah must decide whether loyalty to the institution that made him outweighs the truth that could destroy it. In the end, Jonah trades the secret to a Senate investigator at the cost of his own anonymity, burns Meridian's Lagos file publicly, and walks away stateless but finally belonging to himself.
about_author: Quentin Okonkwo is a former logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between West African ports and European capitals before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be unmemorable.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Between jobs in Vienna, Jonah receives a burner phone he never bought; when it rings, the voice is unmistakably Elias Voss, his mentor, dead two years by official record. Voss says only 'Lagos, midnight, come alone' before the line dies. The beat is cold dread — the past knocking on a door Jonah sealed himself.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah, with a flashback to his recruitment. Jonah reports the call to his handler, Adeyemi, as protocol demands, then watches her lie about it — meaning someone above her already knew. He learns Voss's death certificate was signed by Meridian itself. The emotional beat: the institution that raised him is revealed as something that eats its own.

chapters.title: Midnight in Lagos
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. In Lagos, the meeting is a trap set by someone else entirely: Ruth Voss, Elias's widow, who has been hunting the burner network for months believing it leads to her husband's killers. She shows Jonah a photograph of the massacre site — with Elias alive in the background, dated after his death. Beat: grief weaponized into alliance.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knows
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jonah and Ruth. Ruth reveals Elias went underground after refusing an order tied to the Lagos operation, and that the burner phones are his insurance policy scattered across old contacts. Meridian's cleaners arrive at the safehouse; they escape separately, and Ruth gives Jonah one phone with coordinates. Beat: trust extended under gunfire.

chapters.title: The Cleaner's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Marcus Hale, Meridian's chief cleaner, a man who keeps meticulous records of every job he's buried. Hale is ordered to retrieve the phones and erase everyone connected — including, quietly, Jonah. Through his ledger we learn the massacre was authorized from the top. Beat: chilling professionalism masking a crack of conscience.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Following the coordinates to Prague, Jonah finds not Elias but a dead courier and a phone containing half the Lagos file — enough to implicate Deputy Director Sorren, the man who signed Jonah's first contract. Adeyemi warns him he has twelve hours before Meridian declares him an asset gone dark. Beat: betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours Stateless
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah and Hale in parallel. Jonah races to trade the partial file to Senate investigator Dana Okafor, while Hale closes the net, capturing Ruth as leverage. Jonah realizes the full file — the part naming everyone, including himself — exists only if Elias is alive to surrender it. Beat: the hunter becoming the hunted, guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A staged exchange frees Ruth and delivers Jonah face-to-face with Elias at an abandoned radio station outside Bratislava. Elias admits he let the world bury him to finish the file, and asks Jonah to help him release it — knowing it ends both their careers and exposes Jonah's own role in the cover-up. Beat: the mentor's confession and the son's reckoning.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: POV: all three threads converge. Hale, ordered to kill everyone at the station instead, arrives with Sorren's strike team; Adeyemi defects mid-operation, feeding Jonah the extraction window. Elias is fatally wounded passing Jonah the complete file. Beat: climax — loyalty paid in blood, truth purchased at the highest price.

chapters.title: Signature Required
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah, epilogue six weeks later. Jonah hands Okafor the full file, testifies off-record, and watches Sorren's arrest ripple through Meridian. He buries Elias beside a fabricated name, sends Ruth the ledger page proving her husband died protecting others, and disappears — no country, no handler, no debt. Final beat: belonging, at last, to no one but himself.
